name: Prince Imrahil the Fair
oracle_text: Whenever you draw your second card each turn, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.
blocked_sentences: Whenever you draw your second card each turn, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.

needs.what: A trigger that fires on the *ordinal* of a draw and is decided only where the ability queues -- either a new event (`draw_nth`, with an `nth` field on TriggerSpec so "your second card" is `{"event": "draw_nth", "controller": "you", "nth": 2}`) fired from `draw_cards` in src/automtg/engine/primitives.py when the tally it just bumped equals `nth`, or an equivalent queue-time-only ordinal predicate on the trigger that `resolve_top` does not re-evaluate. Wanted for both polarities, `controller: you` and `controller: opponent`, since the printed template comes in both ("whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn"). Grouping matters here: 47 entries in data/authoring/queue.json print this exact clause -- Alandra Sky Dreamer, Atlantean Cavalry, Bard the Bowman, Bloodhaze Wolverine, Construct a Cosmic Cube, Black Widow Agile Avenger and 41 others -- so one event unblocks the whole family.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The closest existing shape is a `draw` trigger (`controller: "you"`, as isperia.cards.json:937 uses) carrying a `condition` of `{"cmp": "==", "left": {"cards_drawn_this_turn": "you"}, "right": {"const": 2}}`. The value is exactly right at queue time -- primitives.py:44 bumps `state.cards_drawn_this_turn[pid]` immediately *before* the `fire(EventType.DRAW, ...)` on line 45, so the tally read in `triggers._matches` is precisely the ordinal of the draw that just happened. It fails at the other end: a trigger's `condition` is an intervening-if and stack.py:633-644 evaluates it a second time on resolution (rule 603.4), by which point the tally has moved. Concretely -- draw step puts the tally at 1, then any draw-two spell resolves: its first draw takes the tally to 2 and queues the trigger, its second takes the tally to 3 and matches nothing, and when the queued trigger finally resolves the re-check reads 3, returns `skipped="condition"`, and no token is created. Prince Imrahil plus Divination, Brainstorm, or any multi-card draw -- the card's ordinary line of play -- would silently produce nothing. Relaxing the comparison to `>=` and adding `max_per_turn: 1` survives the re-check (the tally is monotonic within a turn and both it and `triggers_this_turn` clear together at untap, turn.py:136-137) and is right in every play pattern I could construct except one: a permanent that enters *after* its controller has already drawn two cards would fire on the next draw, where the printed card does not fire at all that turn. That is a real divergence in a card whose whole text is the trigger, and no gate would catch it, so it is filed rather than shipped. Nothing in `condition_keys` or `value_keys` closes the hole -- the missing piece is not a value, it is a trigger predicate that is not re-asked on resolution.

notes: Single-line card, so there is no expressible remainder to split off: the printed sentence is the trigger and the token, and both halves are blocked. Everything else about the card needs nothing new -- the packet's starting_point already carries the Legendary supertype, Human Noble subtypes, {W}{U}, and 2/2, and no keyword is printed. Order of work: the `draw_second_card_each_turn` event is the one that unblocks 47 queue entries; `human_soldier_token` unblocks this card and three already-filed others.
